state.task: Review five bounded semantic gaps in the current CanLang SaaS draft. Favor economical generation, one canonical primitive, reliable permissions and ordered owner-local workflows. These are proposed draft clarifications, not implemented runtime promises. Assess the supplied alternatives rather than endorsing a presumed winner. No new DTO, authored manifest, compiler implementation, business workflow or infrastructure layer is requested.
state.facts: DESIGN §4 grants reads by row/field union and denies unspecified access; identity/team/parent boundaries remain mandatory. Viewer queries filter permissions before aggregation; mutation rules may inspect authority data without granting it to callers. Pure derives cannot recurse, but the query mode used inside policy predicates is undefined. CanCustomer.has_role queries CompanyRole, whose own policy invokes has_role. Ordinary read=true is viewer-scoped; read=true scope=authority is the existing explicit result grant. DESIGN §§3,5–7 expose record.version and require submitted versions, ordered provisional effects, pre-state locks, final invariants and one authoritative owner. CRUD event.before/input are immutable; event.after is adjustable without invoking the same CRUD again. Scenario writes do not invoke CRUD hooks. Creates in fixtures start at version 1. Migration §11 says conversion advances an affected record once and rename-only preserves its version, but ordinary write/no-op metadata timing is unspecified. Existing scenarios schedule version+1 after set while CRUD hooks schedule event.after.version.
state.workflow: DESIGN §6 aligns every(duration) with UTC epoch, coalesces missed periods, verifies trusted occurrence context and uses null actor for trusted execution; it does not say which team or root-owner receives a tick. Models default to team D1; Durable Object roots route to separate SQLite owners. Eventual root discovery cannot decide authoritative availability. §7 prohibits cross-owner mutation joins and commits receipt, history and outbox atomically with bounded retries. §5 says every failed require rejects the provisional mutation. §6 instead says a false handler guard is skipped. Grammar uses the same require production before and inside do. CanStats trusted examples expect error(rule_failed) on false leading checks; later body checks in other handlers also reject. A send when=false and cancelled/superseded lifecycle work already have skipped outcomes. DeliveryResult already has pending/succeeded/failed/unknown/skipped and DeliveryError carries a safe code/message; do not add a competing status schema.
state.files: DESIGN §8 infers one receiving-app R2 store, immutable finalized files, MIME/content/size/quota checks and attach authority for current app/team/principal or a readable existing attachment. A URL or opaque ID grants no attachment right. Bound capability results may contain file, and successful typed completion is consumed later in its owner transaction. CanPropose and CanInvoice attach PDF result.document, with the actual by and matching guards shown below. Trusted completion has null actor; neither schema checking nor transport success proves file ownership. Finalized but unattached objects already expire after the receipt/attachment horizon. Provider wire mapping and authentication belong to installed adapters, not invented DSL helpers. Preserve exact source guard facts; do not silently add a revision guard missing from CanPropose.
state.research: Official PostgreSQL row-security documentation distinguishes caller-privilege policy expressions from security-definer access; this illustrates a real authority choice, not a required backend. SQLite transaction documentation specifies commit/rollback behavior, not application row-version timing. The research supplies no proof that either proposed CanLang contract is executable. Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html and https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html
state.instruction: Select one alternative for each semantic question, or unresolved if the stated tradeoff is insufficient. Then judge the complete authority/write-intent/fanout/rejection/finalization bundle as a yes/no coherence property. Preserve uncertainty; agreement is advisory and cannot authorize changing user requirements or establish implementation correctness.

code.draft/CanCustomer.can:24-36:
export derive has_role(person:user,org:Customer,role:CompanyRole.role):bool = any(org.CompanyRole as grant,grant.account==person and grant.role==role and grant.active)
  export derive has_location_role(person:user,org:Customer,role:CompanyRole.role,location:Location):bool = any(org.CompanyRole as grant,grant.account==person and grant.role==role and grant.active and location in grant.locations)
  export derive owns(person:user,org:Customer):bool = org.kind==individual and any(org.Contact as contact,contact.account==person and contact.verified)
  derive customer_staff(person:user,org:Customer):bool = any(org.locations as location,can_work(person,location))
  policy Customer read=customer_reader or billing_reader where=customer_staff(actor,row) fields=name,kind,locations,active
  policy Customer read=customer_manager and customer_staff(actor,row)
  policy Customer read=authenticated where=owns(actor,row) or has_role(actor,row,administrator) or has_role(actor,row,booker) or has_role(actor,row,billing)
  policy Contact read=authenticated where=actor.email_verified and row.email==actor.email fields=name,email,account,verified
  policy Contact read=customer_reader or billing_reader where=customer_staff(actor,row.parent) fields=name,email,phone,verified
  policy Contact read=customer_manager and customer_staff(actor,row.parent)
  policy Contact read=authenticated where=row.account==actor or has_role(actor,row.parent,administrator)
  policy CompanyRole read=authenticated where=row.account==actor or has_role(actor,row.parent,administrator)
  policy CompanyRole read=customer_manager and customer_staff(actor,row.parent)
code.draft/CanStats.can:33-47:
scenario process on=WebJobs
   require event.site.active and event.occurred<=now+5m and event.occurred>now-30d
   do
    if not any(event.site.AcceptedEvent as accepted,accepted.event_id==event.event_id)
     create AcceptedEvent {parent=event.site,event_id=event.event_id,name=event.name,occurred=event.occurred,path=event.path,location=event.location,workspace=event.workspace,source=event.source,medium=event.medium,visitor=event.visitor,session=event.session,session_started=event.session_started} as accepted
     send WebDimensions.write {site=event.site.id,name=event.name,path=event.path,location=event.location,source=event.source,value=1} as telemetry
     for health in event.site.Health limit=1
      set health {accepted=health.accepted+1,last_processed=now}
   examples seed=[health] event=WebEvent {site=website,event_id="fresh",name="page_view",occurred=now,path="/"}
    website.active -> health.accepted
    true -> 1
    false -> error(rule_failed)
   examples seed=[health] event=WebEvent {site=website,event_id="expired",name="page_view",occurred=now-30d,path="/"}
    website.active -> health.accepted
    true -> error(rule_failed)
code.draft/CanBook.can:95-104:
scenario ready on=every(1m)
   do
    for appointment in Appointment as item where item.state==pending and item.host_ok and item.room_ok limit=100
     set appointment {state=confirmed}
     send Mail.send {to=appointment.contact.email,subject=format("Appointment confirmed"@{nl="Afspraak bevestigd"},locale=null),body=appointment.parent.parent.instructions} as confirmation
     if appointment.from>now+1h
      schedule appointment.id at=appointment.from-1h event=Reminder {appointment,revision=appointment.version+1}
  scenario remind on=Reminder
   require event.appointment.state==confirmed and event.appointment.version==event.revision
   do send Mail.send {to=event.appointment.contact.email,subject=format("Appointment reminder"@{nl="Afspraakherinnering"},locale=null),body=event.appointment.parent.parent.instructions} when=event.appointment.state==confirmed as notice
code.draft/CanPropose.can:66-75:
scenario document(revision:Revision) by=salesperson or authenticated label=label_QuotePdf_document
   require revision.state in [sent,accepted,declined] and ((salesperson and can_work(actor,revision.parent.location)) or (actor.email_verified and actor.email==revision.recipient_email))
   do
    send Documents.quote {source=revision.id,revision=revision.version,snapshot=QuoteDocument {issuer=revision.issuer_snapshot,recipient=revision.recipient_email,title=revision.title_snapshot,location=revision.location_snapshot,from=revision.from,until=revision.until,terms=revision.terms,expires=revision.expires,lines=revision.Item as item select QuoteLine {title=item.title,quantity=item.quantity,price=item.price,tax=item.tax,discount=item.discount},total=revision.total}} as delivery
    set revision {document_delivery=delivery.id}
  scenario document_result on=Documents.quote.completed
   do
    for revision in Revision as row where row.document_delivery==event.delivery_id limit=1
     if event.status==succeeded and event.result?.source==revision.id
      set revision {pdf=event.result.document}
code.draft/CanInvoice.can:118-126:
require invoice.state==issued and invoice.number!=null and invoice.issued_at!=null and (owns(actor,invoice.parent) or has_role(actor,invoice.parent,billing) or (finance and can_work(actor,invoice.location)))
   do
    send Documents.invoice {source=invoice.id,revision=invoice.version,snapshot=InvoiceDocument {issuer=invoice.issuer,recipient=invoice.recipient,address=invoice.address,tax_reference=invoice.tax_reference,number=invoice.number,issued_at=invoice.issued_at,due=invoice.due,currency=invoice.currency,lines=invoice.Line as line select DocumentLine {title=line.description,quantity=line.quantity,price=line.price,tax=line.tax,discount=line.discount},credits=invoice.Credit as credit select DocumentCredit {amount=credit.amount,reason=credit.reason},payments=invoice.Attempt as payment select DocumentPayment {reference=payment.reference,amount=payment.amount,state=format("{status}",{status=payment.status}),received=payment.received},total=invoice.total}} as delivery
    create DocumentRequest {parent=invoice,revision=invoice.version,delivery=delivery.id} as request
  scenario document_result on=Documents.invoice.completed
   do
    for request in DocumentRequest as row where row.delivery==event.delivery_id limit=1
     if event.status==succeeded and event.result?.source==request.parent.id and event.result.revision==request.revision
      create Document {parent=request.parent,revision=request.revision,file=event.result.document} as document

policy.instructions: Which existing query authority should pure permission predicates inherit?

criteria.authority: Evaluate policy predicates, invariants, locks, CRUD when and mutation/trusted rules with bounded owner authority, retaining team/parent/lifetime limits. A pure derive inherits its entry context; ordinary viewer/read bodies stay filtered, authority-read results require the existing explicit grant. Policy data scans do not recursively apply policies; pure call cycles still fail. This supports grant-table checks without exposing them, but introduces a privileged evaluation mode that must not leak through outputs.
criteria.viewer: Apply viewer filtering to predicate queries as elsewhere and reject recursive policy dependencies. This keeps one query-visibility rule and less privileged evaluation, but CompanyRole/has_role may require app policy restructuring or fail to compile, and hidden grant rows cannot decide permission.
criteria.unresolved: Leave this mode open until a minimal grant-table example proves a safe rule; avoid speculative privilege semantics, accepting that current policy compilation remains blocked.

versions.instructions: Which version contract should existing mutation and hook semantics use?

criteria.write_intent: Create yields version 1 through all same-transaction edits. Existing ordinary aliases keep admission version v while stored fields read proposed writes; any successful set/update/archive targeting the row, even same-value, commits one v+1 and one history/change entry. Hook after projects v+1, before v; repeated writes/calls/hooks add no extra step. Unwritten parents and send-only rows do not advance. This preserves current +1 schedules and hook versions, but no-op assignments cause audit noise and invalidate old references.
criteria.live_dirty: Create stays at 1; an existing row becomes v+1 upon the first normalized value change, stays there for repeated writes or reversions, and untouched/same-value writes keep v. Both ordinary aliases and hook after show this live revision. This avoids no-op conflicts and gives read-through metadata, but current post-set +1 expressions must change and hooks must handle prospective dirty tracking.
criteria.unresolved: Do not pin metadata until focused order/no-op/hook examples settle it. This prevents an unsupported revision choice but leaves reminders, events and target library contracts ambiguous.

ticks.instructions: How should recurring ticks obtain their tenant and atomic-owner context?

criteria.per_scope: Infer the handler scope from its owner-bound model queries/writes. Team D1 handlers receive one occurrence per active team; app-only handlers run once per app; root-bound handlers run per authoritative root instance. Queries stay within that occurrence and incompatible scopes fail. Slot identity includes handler/release, team/owner and epoch; coalescing is per scope, new scopes start next slot. This supports existing team ticks without authored routing, but authoritative scope enumeration and root coverage remain substantial runtime obligations.
criteria.d1_first: Define inferred team/app D1 ticks now but reject root-bound or incompatible recurring handlers; existing record-bound schedule can express supported per-root timing. This reduces the automatic fanout proof burden, but adds explicit arming work for root recurrence and defers a capability of every.
criteria.unresolved: Keep recurring context unselected until a routing example establishes coverage and isolation; this avoids an unproven fanout guarantee while leaving current every handlers non-executable.

requires.instructions: What terminal outcome should a false authored require produce in a trusted handler?

criteria.business_error: Every require, before or inside do, raises its safe business error (default rule_failed), rolls back all provisional effects, and records terminal failed trusted work without retrying that business rejection. Skip is reserved for cancellation, supersession, invalidated/expired lifecycle work and false send when. BDD uses the same actual error path. This preserves Stats expectations and one check meaning, but stale reminders appear as business failures rather than quieter skips.
criteria.leading_skip: Define false leading trusted requires as terminal skipped; false requires inside do remain business failures with whole-operation rollback. Inline examples must expect skipped for the former and update Stats accordingly. This gives stale guards a clean skip, but moving a check across do changes its observable result and two source expectations need revision.
criteria.unresolved: Retain neither conflicting claim as settled pending an explicit outcome decision; no invented error/skip equivalence, but trusted-handler BDD and execution remain blocked.

files.instructions: How should a remote file result become attachable in its receiving owner?

criteria.receiver_finalize: Before successful typed completion, the installed adapter transfers/checks immutable bytes through the receiving app upload/finalization rules. Internal provenance binds app/team/owner, original initiating principal or trusted source, adapter, delivery and result field path; only that completion may attach it without impersonating actor. Stable delivery/path identity reuses checked content on retry and rejects conflicting bytes. Local failure leaves a finalized orphan for existing GC; no cross-storage atomicity. This preserves current PDF types and local policy, but costs transfer/quota and requires adapter finalization work.
criteria.provider_reference: Let file results retain provider-owned immutable storage with a verified delegated right, lifetime and authorized download/attachment contract. This can avoid byte copying, but requires new cross-app file lifetime/permission guarantees beyond the receiving local store and must not accept bare URLs or IDs.
criteria.reject_remote_file: Until a handoff contract exists, reject file-valued remote results. This avoids an unsupported attachment right, but current PDF capability source cannot compile without changing its interface/workflow.
criteria.unresolved: Keep remote file handoff explicitly open while retaining the example shape as non-executable; preserve design uncertainty, accepting that PDF attachments lack a completed authorization contract.

coherence.instructions: Does the combined first option for all five questions form a coherent minimal draft contract that preserves effect order, owner isolation, permission boundaries and actual BDD invocation without pretending implementation exists?

criteria.true: The proposed semantics fit the supplied source facts and boundaries without a concrete contradiction; unfinished enumeration, adaptation and library execution remain acknowledged work.
criteria.false: At least one specific semantic inconsistency or boundary violation prevents recommending this complete bundle, even if its individual choices have useful advantages.
